newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week 3.09 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week 3.09 pct higher.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed on Friday 3.09 percent higher with steady gains all through the week, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 642.30 points from 623.00 last Friday.
"This week there was a renewed interest for privatisation bonds ahead of the flotation of 20 percent of Imiter silver mine next week," a broker said.
The bonds which were issued in January and April last year, give holders preferential options on equity in the privatised firms.

Blue-chip banks such as Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed at 856 dirhans from 798 dirhams, Wafabank gained 35 dirhams during the week to 795 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur was up 70 dirhams to 631 dirhams.
First Moroccan private conglomerate ONA Group closed at 788 dirhams from 762 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, rose 30 dirhams to 730 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir closed at 356.35 dirhams from 349.95 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid advanced 26 dirhams to 549 dirhams.
Credit firm Credor rose 89 dirhams to 771 dirhams and Maroc Leasing shed two dirhams to 427 dirhams. Portfolio firm Financiere Diwan dropped 25 dirhams to 340 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 65.8 from 58.2 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 32.9 million from 147 million dirhams.
